column1: #  page-types.tsv — WHAT EACH PAGE TYPE CARRIES IN ITS MARKUP, AND IF IT IS INDEXED
#  Read by `page-type-gate.pl`. The human source is `blueprint/21-page-types-markup.md`;
#  this is the same table in a form a program reads. The SECTIONS of each type are
#  NOT here: they live in `anatomy.tsv` (09 §2), and this file only points to it.
#  `page-type-gate.pl --tabla` fails if a type of anatomy.tsv has no row here, so
#  a new anatomy cannot be born without saying what it carries in its markup.
#  FORMAT  tipo | alias | anatomia | pagina | obl | rec | prohibido | acciones | indexar | nota
#    tipo       the `data-tipo` value, or what `--tipo` takes
#    alias      other names that mean the same type (space separated)
#    anatomia   the key in anatomy.tsv, or `-` when the type has no measured
#               anatomy yet (its sections are NOT judged until four pages of
#               other businesses are measured, the rule of 09 §2)
#    pagina     the WebPage subtype the page node should be (`WebPage` = none fits)
#    obl        markup the page MUST carry. Groups separated by `;`, and inside a
#               group the alternatives by `/`. A subtype counts (BlogPosting is an
#               Article, Dentist is an Organization). `-` = nothing required
#    rec        recommended, never a failure
#    prohibido  types that must not stand on their own on this page. A node that
#               sits inside an ItemList (`itemListElement`) does not count
#    acciones   the potentialAction types this page may declare, `-` = none
#    indexar    index | noindex | libre
#  Every row is a decision with a reason; the reasons are in blueprint/21 §1-§2.
